answer: Each run of the still is entered in the book, the wash, the cut and the proof, and the spirit must match the entry before any seat is given. A mesa bottle filled in another parish fails the book: at the glacier of the still the proof must match the distiller's own cut, and foreign spirit burns wrong on the tongue. Faking a run means building a still, hiring a distiller and paying 18,900, while the timber entry in the still book is kept by the excise man, so a bottle whose run was never entered is smashed.
